newsitem.title: UK: Tajik security minister taken hostage - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Tajik security minister taken hostage - Tass.

text.p: Tajikistan's Security Minister Saidamir Zukhurov has been taken hostage by rebels holding a group of U.N. workers in the former Soviet republic, Itar-Tass news agency reported on Saturday.

The Russian agency, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, quoted Tajik presidential spokesman Zafar Saidov as saying Zukhurov was seized when he went to the rebels' base camp on Friday for talks on the release of the U.N. personnel.
The United Nations said on Friday it was withdrawing all non-essential personnel from Tajikistan after a spate of kidnappings.

On Thursday, the Red Cross announced it was suspending operations in the Central Asian state after two employees, Elizabeth Trinch of Britain and her Tajik translator, were abducted. They were released on Friday and returned to the Tajik capital Dushanbe.

But four employees with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), including a Nigerian, four U.N. military observers from Austria, Switzerland and Ukraine, and four Russian reporters kidnapped earlier this week were still held by the rebels.
The hostage-takers are part of a group commanded by Rizvon Sadirov, who previously fought for the Islamic opposition forces but whose loyalties are now unclear.
